bindingConstraint.justification: Authority Assignment activity has highest constraint score due to complete absence of formal pathways for Tier 1/2 changes, forcing all changes through heavyweight governance. This creates a structural bottleneck that affects all downstream activities and has maximum intensity (10/10) with high centralization and dependency characteristics.

constraintScoring.selectionRationale: Highest total score (12) among eligible candidates with multiple high-intensity observations and critical downstream dependencies

observations.rationale: No standing governance bodies exist for Tiers 3 and 4, requiring committee reconstitution for each change, creating severe governance friction at Authority Approval stage

evidence.excerpt: No standing governance bodies exist for Tiers 3 and 4, requiring committee reconstitution for each change

observations.rationale: No propagation mechanism exists to cascade constitutional changes to dependent systems and instances, creating handoff failure at System Propagation stage

bindingConstraint.justification: Authority Approval activity represents the binding constraint due to absence of standing governance bodies for Tiers 3 and 4, requiring committee reconstitution for each change. This creates high authority centralization and significant downstream dependencies, as no subsequent constitutional changes can proceed without governance approval.

constraintScoring.selectionRationale: Highest total score (10) with critical authority centralization and downstream dependency characteristics
